comments.value: I have a minimal reproduction project available if needed.
Can you attach the reproduction project?
Alternatively (probably better), can you provide an affected avatar ID?
you can try it yourself at https://vrchat.com/home/avatar/avtr_29fece6f-edf6-4f2a-a1f8-f59fc1d6d683

The top displayed value is synced and controlled from the menu.

The bottom displayed value is derived from the top one using a 1d blendtree, and SHOULD display 1 minus the top value. It has a noop clip at input = 1, and a "display 1" clip at input = 0.

However, on remotes, since the resting state of the bottom display gets "rebaked" as 1, and the 1d blendtree only has a clip that outputs 1, it always displays one on remotes.

I can also confirm this is happening. People keep telling me my avatars are broken even though I haven't changed the FX at all, I only turned on the new FT system. Anything operating on those defaults, like empty off states or additive layers, is affected. I'm converting all of my avatars back to the old system until this is fixed. :(
unfortunately this is very widespread and quite critical

Yep, I can confirm this on my end. Extremely critical issue as many said. I am updating my avatar base to use Native FT and save on hundreds of parameter bits, however ever since I turned the feature on it catastrophically broke only for remote players. Gesture animations get stuck for them on whichever one was active on avatar load. It also broke some puppet features it has. I even had a mental breakdown trying to figure out what was wrong, until I saw this post and suddenly it all made sense.

I am forced to do many workarounds just to get around this game breaking bug, which I would love to avoid doing (adds quite some unnecessary complexity). Please fix this!
a lot of people have been seeing things toggled differently on my avatar since i changed to native face tracking, can confirm

Heyyyyy more types of issues with Native FT now. I have an avi where it is half way in the ground only for remote players, which immediately made me think of this bug. The moment I disabled Native FT it went back to normal. How is that even possible?

I sometimes question if they actually tested the feature properly before shipping it. There's no way that an update can manage to critically break so many avis simply by enabling a new feature that looks completely unrelated to said issues. The feature currently feels like they've coded it, then simply tested the face tracking alone without ensuring that the rest of the avatar works for both local and remote players (the latter can be hard to troubleshoot for the typical player without the right equipment) and threw it immediately to the live branch.

I will be honest, you might want to bring back the feature to cook for a little longer. This is clearly not production ready.

UPDATE: Just saw the Open Beta with a supposed patch for this bug (at least that's what it eludes to). Unfortunately the avi I mentioned in my last comment still sinks in the floor for remote clients only, and only when Native FT is enabled. Keep digging, something serious broke with this new feature.
@{6074413eb2699d0dae05d4f7|full_name}: Do you have an avatar id that you could share for the affected avatar?

@{6161a61a2c0de966b4e43486|full_name} The affected avatar's TOS forbids distributing as a public, and also contains a yet to be released DLC asset for it (they cannot be separated). So unfortunately I cannot give the ID specific to this one. I might have some theories though since it's an expanded version of a base where it has some extra non-humanoid bones for an updated mesh and a different Blender FBX export scale (100x instead of 1x), all reconfigured in a new unique Prefab. Everything else is the exact same.

If I just take the FBX, scale it correctly (Scale Factor 1 + Convert Units OFF in FBX settings, scale 1 prefab root object and the armature root inside it), put the Descriptor with correct View Position and turn Native FT on, it goes in the floor in-game only for remote players. If I turn it off, it's fine again. In comparison, the original non-edited base doesn't have this specific issue.

It's midnight here, so won't be able to try and make a demo with a replica of the issue just yet. If I do I will ping again (maybe what I provided here could be enough to troubleshoot on your end)

Native FT off: avtr_440c4470-a623-416f-a5f6-f25a2cc71163

details:
It seems that, on avatars with FT enabled, remote clients run the animator for a frame, and then improperly re-record all of the animator default values (perhaps because the animator is being toggled or reset improperly or otherwise). This issue ONLY happens on remote clients, not on local. The bug seems to require Face Tracking to be configured with a target mesh and a few valid blendshapes AND for Eye Look to be enabled (even if it's not configured in a FT eye look mode).

This breaks many avatar systems, since the basis state of the avatar contains all of the "unanimated" defaults, and many controllers (especially those with WD on) only have clips which target the opposite of that state.

This is likely the root cause of the recent partially-weighted AAP and sync parameter issues reported regarding FT (although I don't believe it's actually a sync issue).
title: Animator Defaults are improperly changed, only on remote clients, when native FT is configured
